description: "WEV-4154 — native GrowthOS completions sent the owner-only resume URL when the share link was created seconds later; fixed by wevo-pulse #952; 8 past completions not re-sent; prod evidence queries"

GrowthOS stores `pulseLink` once, from wevo-pulse's `pulse.findings_completed` webhook (`org_webhook_event.payload_json`). Before #952 (merged 2026-10-28, squash 1bed2f1c), native Pulses sent `/share/pulse/<link>` only if a `pulse_public_share_link` row already existed, else the authenticated `/pulse?pulseId=` resume URL. That URL opens only for the owner: other project members (same Accenture org) got an in-frame login or "Pulse unavailable". The owner's share dialog usually created the link 2 to 30 s after completion. 8 of 68 delivered completions were affected (Compares 26899d48, 20653c5c, d46b2c29; Pulses 80aeb500, 3bdb9561, faa01987, fb3112b5, 9f54798b). Customer API never had this because it creates a share link at Pulse creation.

**Why:** "Compare share URLs need auth" turned out to be URL selection plus a race. Compare permissions were fine: Accenture users have the `compare_user` org role.

**How to apply:** for GrowthOS "can't open Pulse" reports, query `org_webhook_event` (`event_type='pulse.findings_completed'`, `payload_json->>'pulseLink'`) against `pulse_public_share_link.created_at` first. A re-send changes the GrowthOS idempotency key (it includes pulseLink) and may double-charge credits, so the past 8 were left alone. Open follow-ups: customer-app login drops pulseId (Done-when #2), and "Load in Wevo" stays owner-only. See [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]].

- Since #951/#953 (2026-10-28), `make finish-work` runs targeted `make code-quality` over the branch (merge base with origin/main, plus dirty and untracked files) and writes `validation.command: make code-quality`. It takes about 1 min. PR CI and the merge queue own the full suite. Don't set `CODE_QUALITY_BACKEND_WORKERS` or `FINISH_WORK_SCOPE=full`, and don't run detached gate or retry loops. A local full suite now queues for a machine-wide slot.
- **Why:** on 2026-10-28, several sessions each ran the old ~40–60 min full suite at once. Load hit about 50 on 12 cores, which caused browser and timing flakes, and the user had another session SIGTERM the runs.
- A fresh worktree has no backend venv: `cd backend && uv sync --frozen --extra dev`. Rerun `uv sync --extra dev` after a rebase that changes deps (pytest-timeout was added 2026-10-28).
- Each finish-work attempt with `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` set leaves a pending receipt. The final clean run finalizes all of them into identical `changesets/patch/YYYY-MM/*.yaml` fragments. Keep only the newest one and delete the rest before committing.
- The backend-complexity gate fails if a module's radon MI rank drops (e.g. growthos_pulse_webhooks.py was 19.90 A, so adding a few lines made it B). Move new logic into a smaller module rather than rewriting the baseline.
- `tests/test_dev_provider_preflight.py` shells out to `python3`. On this Mac, Homebrew's python3 has no PyYAML, so put `backend/.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- The tracked `.husky/_/*` Entire hooks call `~/.local/bin/entire`, which was moved (only `entire-0.9.0.bak` remains). Commits fail in fresh worktrees, so use `git commit --no-verify`. There's no pre-commit lint hook to skip.
- `tests/test_capture_resize_isolation.py` flakes under load. See [[wevo-pulse-ci-browser-test-flakes]].

**How to apply:** rebase, `uv sync --extra dev`, then run `make finish-work` once in the background, commit the newest fragment, and push. Let CI run the full suite.

name: wevo-pulse-ci-browser-test-flakes
description: wevo-pulse "CI and Dev Release" backend shards flake on browser-capture timing tests under runner load; rerun failed jobs rather than debugging
metadata:
  type: project
---

The wevo-pulse GitHub Actions workflow "CI and Dev Release" splits the backend
suite into 4 shards (about 4,900 tests each, 10 to 19 minutes). Shards 1 and 3
carry most of the Playwright/Chromium capture tests and fail intermittently on
timing or deadline assertions that have nothing to do with the PR under test.
Seen 2026-10-17 on PR #908 (legacy quant findings change, no capture code
touched): attempt 1 failed `test_navigation_redundant_capture` (preload scroll
restore timeout), `decisions_research_capture/test_initial_reload`, and
`decisions_research_capture/test_noop_origin` (got `research_capture_deadline`);
attempt 2 passed all three but failed `test_paths_empty_capture` on cookie
consent dismissal; attempt 3 was green. Flakes cluster when several runs share
the runner pool (two main pushes were running concurrently).

The gating job is "CI required", which just checks the validate and
runtime-image results. Branch protection and rulesets cannot be read via API
(repo is private without GitHub Pro). Recent merges to main are squash merges
done by ryan-d-bigelow, with `delete_branch_on_merge` off.

**Why:** A red shard on a PR that does not touch `backend/app/services/legacy/decisions_research_capture.py`, `population_navigation`, or `goal_navigation_handler` is almost certainly runner load, not a regression. Prior commits on main ("isolate ... from CI scheduling", "Stabilize ... deadline tests under CI load") show this is a known class.

**How to apply:** Pull the failing test names from the job log first. If they are capture/deadline/consent tests outside the PR's diff, use `gh run rerun <run-id> --failed` (keeps the passing shards and the Cursor approval) and wait about 15 minutes, up to a couple of times. Only investigate if the same test fails twice or the PR touches capture code. Merge with `gh pr merge --squash`. Note `gh` is at `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`, not on the default PATH in this harness.

- Dev deploy job of a main push run (CI and Dev Release): `gh run rerun --failed` always fails with "Immutable image artifact is not owned by this exact attempt"; use a full `gh run rerun <id>` (rebuilds the image in the new attempt). Seen 2026-10-18 on run 39165918107 (attempt 1 exit 137 on a worker-pod fleet_healthcheck exec; attempt 3 full rerun green). Also flaky on PR backend shards: decisions_research_capture test_document_origin / test_final_filtered_capture.
- **Never `gh run rerun --failed` a main push run when the Dev deploy matters** (learned 2026-10-19, run 39330959794): the Dev deploy job (`verify_same_run_dev_image.py fetch-owner`) rejects an image built by an earlier attempt ("Immutable image artifact is not owned by this exact attempt"). Rerun the whole run (`gh run rerun <id>` without `--failed`) so the image is rebuilt in the same attempt; the run stays `event=push`, which the Stage release candidate check needs.

def _resume_url(pulse: LegacySession) -> str | None:

def _share_url(session: Session, pulse: LegacySession) -> str | None:
    from app.services.pulse_share_link_mutation import add_native_link  # noqa: PLC0415

    shares = session.exec(
        select(PulseShareLink)
        .where(
            col(PulseShareLink.pulse_id) == pulse.id,
            col(PulseShareLink.pulse_type) == PulseShareLinkPulseType.LEGACY_SESSION.value,
        )
        .order_by(col(PulseShareLink.created_at).asc())
    ).all()
    share = next((row for row in shares if row.deleted_at is None), None)
    if not shares:
        # GrowthOS gives this link to every project member; the resume URL opens
        # only for the owner. Customer API likewise shares every Pulse it creates.

            pulse_type=PulseShareLinkPulseType.LEGACY_SESSION,
            org_id=pulse.org_id,
            actor_subject_id=pulse.owner_sub or pulse.created_by_sub or "system",

def _complete(db: Session, pulse: LegacySession) -> dict[str, Any]:
    pulse.state = LegacySessionState.FINDINGS_READY.value
    db.add(pulse)
    db.commit()
    completion = db.exec(
        select(OrgWebhookEvent).where(
            col(OrgWebhookEvent.event_type) == WebhookEventType.PULSE_FINDINGS_COMPLETED

    assert completion.error_summary is None
    return completion.payload_json

`GROWTHOS_WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD_MODE=auto` is an explicit transition mode. It first sends the full payload, then on HTTP 400 for `pulse.findings_completed` immediately retries with the six-field legacy completion body below. That event retains its legacy projection for later retries, while every new event starts with the full payload again. The other five events have no legacy equivalent. Their HTTP 400 responses remain failed attempts and follow the bounded retry policy; they must never be converted into a completion or a billing transaction.

`expanded` sends full payloads without fallback. Both `auto` and `expanded` require `GROWTHOS_WEBHOOK_EXPANDED_PRODUCTION_APPROVED=true` for a production runtime or the production partner hostname because both can emit the expanded schema. That flag defaults false. The application default is `legacy`. Environment-specific desired configuration and actual deployment are separate facts; do not infer either from this default. Exercise `auto` or `expanded` only with a controlled receiver or a compatible staging endpoint.

The legacy completion projection has exactly six keys:

```json
{
  "userId": "owner@example.com",
  "projectId": "growthos-project-123",
  "name": "Checkout flow",
  "pulseLink": "https://beta.wevo.ai/pulse/sessions/share-link-123?hideHeader=true&hideAssistant=true&hideSidebar=true",
  "cost": 1,
  "reportType": "pulse"
}
```

## Links and the existing Discover action

`resumeUrl` is an authenticated deep link, preserving GrowthOS presentation and the two separate identifiers. It does not grant access to the Pulse. `pulseLink`/`findingsShareUrl` refer only to an existing active public share and include the GrowthOS presentation. They may be null if a share has not yet been created. Completion does not create a public share implicitly or bypass its authorization.

Customer App's existing **Send to Discover** dialog creates/copies a public report link for the user to paste into Discover. Clicking it is not an automatic webhook delivery acknowledgement. The automatic completion event can precede that dialog and therefore carry a null public link. The partner's null-link policy and any later link update must be agreed before claiming that the entire receiving workflow is ready.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ryanbigelow/.claude-easycliproxy/skills/sol-loop

# sol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use OpenAI's GPT Sol to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the Sol reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. Sol must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start Sol

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest Sol unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native Sol subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run Sol. If no route runs Sol, report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell Sol: open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with sol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Sol verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what Sol changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.

**Merged (Claude, 10-29)**

PRs
- wevo-pulse #955 (https://github.com/wevo-conversion/wevo-pulse/pull/955), squash `772c3e72`, on main
- customer-app #2985 (https://github.com/wevo-conversion/customer-app/pull/2985), squash `cb5c07a7`, on staging

Root cause: GrowthOS stores `pulseLink` once at completion. `_share_url` hardcoded `hideAssistant=true`, and since #952 completion also creates the share with `share_assistant_chat=false`. Every new GrowthOS link would hide Persona Chat for good.

Fix
- wevo-pulse: the share that completion creates turns on the owner's Assistant chat (`chat_shared_by_subject_id` = owner, who also owns the public conversation). `pulseLink` drops `hideAssistant`, so the share row's own setting decides and a later toggle reaches links already stored. Existing shares are reused unchanged. Pulses with no owner keep chat off. `docs/growthos-integration.md` updated.
- customer-app: under the GrowthOS theme, opening Send to Discover on a WEVO Pulse report PATCHes `shareAssistantChat: true` if it's off, and hides the toggle. The URL stays in "Loading share URL…" until that resolves, so a `hideAssistant=true` link can't be copied mid-request. Classic theme unchanged.

Proof
- Backend: updated assertions fail on the old code and pass with the fix. 173 GrowthOS tests green after rebase, `make finish-work` clean, CI green.
- Frontend: new `PulseHeader.rootRoute.test.tsx` case fails without the change, including the pending-PATCH copy guard. `yarn code-quality` and CI green.
- Real browser (visual-baseline harness, mocked APIs): GrowthOS dialog sent PATCH `{shareAssistantChat:true}`, rendered no toggle, URL ended `hideAssistant=false`. Classic dialog still showed the toggle, sent no PATCH, and kept `hideAssistant=true`.
- Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds, gpt-6.1-sol, approved (one finding fixed: the copy-before-PATCH race).

Deploy state
- Not in Stage or prod yet. **Do not deploy wevo-pulse tag 0.1.233 to prod by itself**: it has #952 without this fix, so every new GrowthOS link would hide chat. Cut the next release from main (contains both #952 and `772c3e72`). customer-app needs a release from staging containing `cb5c07a7`.

Open items
- Verified in production: not done. Prod kube API was unreachable from here (VPN down).
- Links already stored in GrowthOS with `hideAssistant=true` (e.g. Jessica's Oct 27-28 Pulses) still hide chat. Restoring them needs a GrowthOS-side link update or a customer-app override; out of scope here.
- customer-api-backed reports still force `hideAssistant=true` (out of scope per ticket).

**Fix merged via WEV-4197 (Claude, 10-29)**

Implements the decision (GrowthOS users get Persona Chat by default): wevo-pulse #955 (`772c3e72`) and customer-app #2985 (`cb5c07a7`). Details, proof, and deploy notes are on WEV-4197. Neither is deployed yet. Don't ship wevo-pulse 0.1.233 alone: it has #952 without this fix.

Still open on this ticket
- Prod check of Jessica's 3 Pulses (project 66d63523-5d34-41a1-b992-aebc2b446417): not done. The prod kube API timed out from here (VPN down). The queries in the first comment are still the ones to run.
- Links GrowthOS already stored for her Oct 27-28 Pulses carry `hideAssistant=true`, so the fix won't bring chat back on those. New Pulses after deploy get chat.
- Reply to Kerry, and an answer on Jessica's credit request: not done (customer-facing, needs a human).

content.text:
Both fixes are on Stage, and every step of the Stage pipeline passed on the first try. For the prod release, use **Pulse 0.1.234** (not 0.1.233) and **customer-app 0.1.288** or later. Nothing has gone to prod.

I haven't confirmed the fix on Stage with real data yet. I only have proof that the deploys succeeded.

**Merged**
- wevo-pulse [#955](https://github.com/wevo-conversion/wevo-pulse/pull/955), squash commit `772c3e72`: when a GrowthOS Pulse completes, the share link we create now has Persona Chat turned on. The link we send to GrowthOS no longer carries `hideAssistant=true`, so the share's own chat setting decides whether chat shows.
- customer-app [#2985](https://github.com/wevo-conversion/customer-app/pull/2985), squash commit `cb5c07a7`: in GrowthOS, Send to Discover turns chat on and shows no toggle. The link can't be copied until chat is on. Outside GrowthOS nothing changed.

**On Stage now**
- **Pulse 0.1.234**, built from `772c3e72`, has both #952 and this fix. I waited for that commit's own CI run, including the Dev deploy, then ran release 40900828647, credit audit 40904708032, and scheduler activation 40905115817. It replaces the 0.1.233 that was on Stage, which had #952 without the fix.
- **customer-app 0.1.288** (release 40895902837) contains `cb5c07a7` and #2984, which was already merged. Stage started serving it at 15:02 UTC.

**Proof**
- **Backend tests:** the updated tests fail on the old code and pass with the fix. 173 GrowthOS tests pass, the repo's full quality gate (`make finish-work`) passes, and CI is green.
- **Frontend test:** the new test fails without the change, including the check that the link can't be copied before chat is on. `yarn code-quality` and CI are green.
- **Real browser, mocked APIs:**
  - In the GrowthOS theme, opening Send to Discover turned chat on, showed no toggle, and the link ended in `hideAssistant=false`.
  - In the classic theme, the toggle was still there and the link still hid chat.
  - Screenshots are in `/Users/ryanbigelow/source/wevo/repos/output/wev-4197/`.
- **Review:** GPT Sol reviewed both diffs over 2 rounds and approved. It found one real bug: a link could be copied before chat was turned on. I fixed it.

**Not done**
- **Real-data check on Stage:** the Stage kube login expired on Oct 26 and needs your browser to refresh, and checking the Stage UI needs a human sign-in. The quickest check is to finish one GrowthOS Pulse on Stage. Its link should have no `hideAssistant`, and opening it should show the chat.
- **Prod check of Jessica's 3 Pulses:** prod was unreachable from here because the VPN is down.
- **Jessica's existing links:** the ones GrowthOS already stored for her Oct 27–28 Pulses still include `hideAssistant=true`, so they'll keep hiding chat. Only new Pulses get chat.
- **Customer follow-up:** the reply to Kerry and the answer on Jessica's credit request are still open for a person to handle.

**Decisions I made**
- Pulses with no owner keep chat off, so a chat conversation is never owned by the placeholder "system" account.
- Existing share links are left as they are. Only links created at completion turn chat on automatically.

Org `org_Nik2XGWIuvXhmqtQ` = company 136, team 138; `pulse_user` role carries `access:pulse3.0`, so Accenture creates native Pulses in wevo-pulse since ~2026-09-24.

- Aurora users live in `wevo."user"` (singular, quoted; column `email_address`, citext), not `users`; team links in `wevo.team_to_user`. ---
name: wevo-prod-access-and-topology
description: How to inspect WEVO Pulse/customer-app production and stage read-only (AWS profiles, kube contexts, CLIs, hostnames, deploy workflows)
metadata:
  type: reference
---

- Shell PATH in this harness is minimal; CLIs live in `/opt/homebrew/bin` (aws, gh, terraform, auth0, uv, node) and `/usr/local/bin/kubectl`. There is no global `yarn`; wevo-access (node ^22, yarn 3.6.4 via packageManager) needs `PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.0/bin:$PATH COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0` so its husky pre-commit (`yarn lint-staged` + `make code-quality`, ~3 min) can run instead of being bypassed.
- AWS: profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai` = prod account 900670598745; `duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai` / `nonprod` = nonprod 380283542572 (ECR for both lives in 380283542572, region us-east-1). `default` = legacy account 844859623362.
- Kube contexts `prod` (duploinfra-prod) and `nonprod`; namespaces `duploservices-prod` / `duploservices-stage`. Pulse backend deployments are `personas-api`, `personas-api-beat`, `personas-api-worker-*`; env comes from k8s secrets `<app>-env-config` and `<app>-secrets`, which mirror SSM `/<tenant>/personas-api/env/{config,secrets}` (secret values are placeholder-created by Terraform and populated manually).
- Hostnames: prod Pulse API `https://personas-api.wevo.ai`, Pulse SPA `https://personas.wevo.ai`, customer-app `https://app.wevo.ai`; stage API `https://personas-api-stage.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai`, customer-app `https://staging-app.wevo.ai`. `prod.sandbox.wevo.ai` in customer-app `.env.production` is stale (TLS cert does not cover it); the real prod build reads SSM `/prod/customer-app/env/config`.
- Deploys: wevo-pulse "Deploy to Prod" workflow (workflow_dispatch from main with `release_tag`; migrations run from the release image before rollout); customer-app "Deploy to Prod" (dispatch from `staging` with a release tag). There is no `master`/`production` branch in use for customer-app; prod is a staging tag.
- Local targeted Terraform against nonprod tenant roots works with `DUPLO_HOST=https://duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai DUPLO_TENANT=<dev|stage> AWS_PROFILE=duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai` and `DUPLO_TOKEN` read from `~/.duplo/cache/duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai,admin,duplo-creds.json` (check its `Expiration`; refresh with `duploctl --interactive`). Git-sourced modules need GitHub SSH (works). `-target` pulls in dependencies, so plan from a branch that includes current main or you will see reverts of newer applied changes. The `auth0` CLI's `wevo-staging` tenant login is broken (refresh_token grant not allowed); `wevo-dev` works via `--tenant wevo-dev.us.auth0.com`.
- `auth0` CLI is logged in with tenant `wevo-prod.us.auth0.com` active; `auth0 roles list --json`, `auth0 roles permissions list <id> --json`, `auth0 api get roles/<id>/users` work read-only.

**How to apply:** use these for read-only production evidence before claiming anything is deployed or configured. See [[figma-oauth-prod-rollout-2026-10]].
---
name: growthos-completion-link-race-2026-10
description: "WEV-4154 — native GrowthOS completions sent the owner-only resume URL when the share link was created seconds later; fixed by wevo-pulse #952; 8 past completions not re-sent; prod evidence queries"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2b6c2df7-16ca-40d0-b24f-5ed1573620da
  modified: 2026-10-28T22:58:19.994Z
---

GrowthOS stores `pulseLink` once, from wevo-pulse's `pulse.findings_completed` webhook (`org_webhook_event.payload_json`). Before #952 (merged 2026-10-28, squash 1bed2f1c), native Pulses sent `/share/pulse/<link>` only if a `pulse_public_share_link` row already existed, else the authenticated `/pulse?pulseId=` resume URL. That URL opens only for the owner: other project members (same Accenture org) got an in-frame login or "Pulse unavailable". The owner's share dialog usually created the link 2 to 30 s after completion. 8 of 68 delivered completions were affected (Compares 26899d48, 20653c5c, d46b2c29; Pulses 80aeb500, 3bdb9561, faa01987, fb3112b5, 9f54798b). Customer API never had this because it creates a share link at Pulse creation.

**Why:** "Compare share URLs need auth" turned out to be URL selection plus a race. Compare permissions were fine: Accenture users have the `compare_user` org role.

**How to apply:** for GrowthOS "can't open Pulse" reports, query `org_webhook_event` (`event_type='pulse.findings_completed'`, `payload_json->>'pulseLink'`) against `pulse_public_share_link.created_at` first. A re-send changes the GrowthOS idempotency key (it includes pulseLink) and may double-charge credits, so the past 8 were left alone. Open follow-ups: customer-app login drops pulseId (Done-when #2), and "Load in Wevo" stays owner-only. See [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]].

**Follow-up (2026-10-29, WEV-4197):** #952 made every completion link hide Persona Chat (share created with chat off + hardcoded `hideAssistant=true`). Fixed by wevo-pulse #955 (`772c3e72`, completion share turns chat on for the owner; link drops `hideAssistant`) and customer-app #2985 (`cb5c07a7`, GrowthOS Send to Discover auto-enables chat, no toggle). Tag 0.1.233 has #952 without #955, so never deploy 0.1.233 to prod alone. Links GrowthOS stored earlier with `hideAssistant=true` still hide chat.

**Prod check: Jessica's Pulses (read-only, pulse_db, 2026-10-29 18:15 UTC)**

All 9 Pulses in GrowthOS project 66d63523 are native wevo-pulse sessions owned by Jessica. Prod Pulse API is 0.1.231, so neither #952 nor #955 is live yet.

| Pulse | Created (UTC) | Share row chat | Link GrowthOS stored |
|---|---|---|---|
| dab57f7b | Oct 6 | off | none (webhook failed: `required_userId_missing`) |
| 9d68c4eb | Oct 12 21:09 | off | `/share/pulse/7NRf…?hideHeader&hideAssistant=true&…` |
| e09db610, 8337f12e | Oct 27 | **on** | `…hideAssistant=true…` |
| 9dcca195, 68f2d6d2, 658729e6, 6318e2bc | Oct 28 | **on** | `…hideAssistant=true…` |
| 687f27c9 | Oct 29 | **on** | `…hideAssistant=true…` |

What this shows:
* **The stored link never showed chat, including on Oct 12.** Every `pulse.findings_completed` payload (`pulseLink` and `findingsShareUrl`) has `hideAssistant=true`. Every payload, Oct 12 included, also has the same authenticated `resumeUrl` (`/pulse?pulseId=…&theme=growthos`).
* **Nothing changed in our code between the two dates.** Customer-app prod was 0.1.258 on Oct 12 and 0.1.281 on Oct 27–28. In both, the shared page and the signed-in findings page decide whether to show the Assistant the same way (`!hideAssistant && …`).
* So the chat Jessica saw on Oct 12 most likely came from the signed-in `resumeUrl` view, which shows the Assistant to the owner, not from the stored link. Which URL GrowthOS shows is decided on their side, and we can't see it.
* **The Oct 12 delivery was the only one that didn't go through first time.** GrowthOS answered the first attempt with HTTP 500 and accepted the retry 69 s later. Every later delivery succeeded on the first attempt. That could have kept her on the `resumeUrl` view, but it's unproven.
* **She already turned chat on.** From Oct 27, every share row has `share_assistant_chat=true` with Jessica as the chat owner. So she used "Include Assistant chat" in Send to Discover, but the stored `hideAssistant=true` overrides it.

**What the fix changes once Pulse 0.1.234 is in prod** (customer-app 0.1.288 went to prod 16:24 UTC today; the Pulse 18:08 run only validated and prepared the image):
* **New GrowthOS completions:** links have no `hideAssistant`, and chat is on for the owner.
* **Links already stored**, including all of Jessica's: they keep `hideAssistant=true` and still hide chat. The fix only reaches them if we either re-send the completion webhook (new idempotency key, risk of double-charging credits) or have customer-app let the share's chat setting win over `hideAssistant` for `theme=growthos`. Jessica's 7 Pulses from Oct 27 onward already have chat on, so that second option would restore them with no data change. It needs a decision.

Pulse **0.1.234** is rolling out to prod, and the new pods have the fix. The deploy run (40928101072) is still in its final checks, so I don't have a final result yet.

**Prod state right now (18:21 UTC):**
- **API pods:** 0.1.234 pods are replacing the 0.1.231 ones, and the new pods include the fix (`growthos_pulse_webhooks.py:131`, `share_assistant_chat=bool(owner)`).
- **Workers:** all are on 0.1.234. That includes `worker-legacy-findings`, which sends the completion webhook.
- **Scheduler (`personas-api-beat`):** it crashed three times on startup (exit code 2) and is now running. My guess is it was waiting for the old scheduler to let go, which a later check in the deploy run covers. That's unconfirmed, because its earlier logs were empty.
- **Deploy run:** it's on "Require complete Pulse rollout". After that come the scheduler, worker heartbeat and GrowthOS config checks.
- **customer-app:** 0.1.288 has been in prod since 16:24 UTC.

**Verified in prod:** not yet. No GrowthOS Pulse has completed in the last 3 hours, so nothing has gone through the new code. Unlike on Stage, I won't run the share-link code against a real prod Pulse, even in a rolled-back transaction, without your approval. The real check is the next GrowthOS completion: its `pulseLink` should have no `hideAssistant` and its share row should have chat on.

**Still needs a decision from you:** links already stored, including Jessica's, will still hide chat. The fix I'd suggest is a customer-app rule: under the GrowthOS theme, the share's own chat setting wins over `hideAssistant`. Jessica's 7 Pulses from Oct 27 onward already have chat on, so that would restore them with no data change.

If you'd like, I can come back once the deploy run finishes to confirm its result and look for the first GrowthOS completion on 0.1.234.

# sol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use OpenAI's GPT Sol to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the Sol reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. Sol must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start Sol

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest Sol unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native Sol subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run Sol. If no route runs Sol, report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell Sol: open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with sol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Sol verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what Sol changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.

**Fix for links GrowthOS already stored: merged and verified on Stage**

customer-app #2987 (squash `8ba68789`, Stage 0.1.289): under the GrowthOS theme, the shared Pulse page ignores the URL's `hideAssistant=true` and the share's own chat setting decides. Links GrowthOS stored before WEV-4197 now show Persona Chat wherever the owner has chat on. No data change and no webhook re-send. Proof:
* Two new unit tests (GrowthOS link stored with `hideAssistant=true`, chat on / chat off) fail without the fix. All 158 SharedFindingsPage tests pass, `yarn code-quality` is green, and Sol review approved in round 1.
* Stage 0.1.289, real public links in a headless browser:
  * GrowthOS stored-style link (`hideAssistant=true&theme=growthos`) on a share with chat on: Assistant shown.
  * The same URL on a share with chat off: hidden.
  * Same share with chat on, without the GrowthOS theme: no Assistant request, hidden.

Prod impact once customer-app 0.1.289 is in prod: Jessica's 7 Pulses from Oct 27 onward have chat on, so their stored links will show chat. Her Oct 12 Pulse had chat off and would need it turned on in Send to Discover. Prod is on customer-app 0.1.288 and Pulse 0.1.234; releasing 0.1.289 to prod is pending approval.
